The gtable panel drawn at a facet panel's place in the grid

Source: R/ggplot2_facet_utils.R
map_visual_to_dom_panel.Rd

ggplot2 reports where it lays each facet panel out as ROW and COL in built$layout$layout, and names the panels of the gtable it draws panel-<a>-<b>. What a and b count is not the row and the column, and differs between facets and releases. ggplot2 3.4.4 and 3.5 name a facet_grid() panel panel-<row>-<col>, but write the facet_wrap() names in an order that matches no grid: a 2 x 2 wrap is panel-<row>-<col>, a 2 x 3 one has panel-3-1 in the first row, second column. ggplot2 4.0 names a wrap's panels panel-<col>-<row>. Reading the name as the column- major position of the panel, as this did, gave each 2 x 2 wrap and grid the two off-diagonal panels each other's names, and most panels of a grid that is not square another panel's name, so their selectors named the marks of another panel: the highlight lit the other panel's marks, and maidr.js, which places a subplot where its first mark is drawn, put the subplots out of order.

Usage

map_visual_to_dom_panel(panel_info, gtable)

Arguments

panel_info

Panel information from layout

gtable

Gtable object

Value

Gtable panel name or NULL if not found

Details

What every release keeps is where a panel is drawn: its row and column in the gtable's layout, t and l. A panel's rank among the distinct t of the panels is its row, and its rank among the distinct l its column, whatever the gtable calls it. A place no panel is drawn at names none: guessing at another panel would hand the layer that panel's marks, as find_gtable_panel_grob() declines to.
